name: Harry and Caroline (Evening Standard, 24 and 28 March 1863) and Tissie and Jabber (Daily Mail, 14 and 16 Sept 1901) advertisements
ciphertext: CAROLINE. - Gd kzd lgsuoabzbt. Hjf pw Ebcvgfm, klv slxdzp t ugwxbz. - Harry.
HARRY. - U ponngf qw. G xtab io cwldf. Zhnc vh xwcd. - CAROLINE
TISSIE. - Dano dbno dcno ddno dona donb donc donc dond onad onbd oncd ondd. - JABBER
JABBER. - Nado nbdo ncdo nddo anod bnod cnod dnod onad. TISSIE
ciphertext_source: Cipherbrain post 30 (Schmeh 2017, sources/schmeh/posts/30-harry-caroline.txt) after Jean Palmer (Tony Gaffney), The Agony Column Codes & Ciphers; British Newspaper Archive images exist behind a paywall (owner route).
alphabet: a-z with word breaks and punctuation kept; Harry 44 letters, Caroline 27; Tissie-Jabber: only d, o, n, a, b, c

constraints.single_letter_words: t (Harry), U and G (Caroline) must be a or I under a MASC
constraints.tissie_jabber: four-letter groups over d o n a b c in an exhaustive-looking order: an enumeration (a betting or meeting-time code, Ernst 2015), not prose; the reply lists the n?do / ?nod forms the first ad omits

cheap_tests_in_order: 1. MASC with word boundaries on Harry+Caroline jointly (71 letters), single-letter words fixed to a/I, the capitalised 'Ebcvgfm' tried as a name; judge in en. Control: an English 71-letter text with the same word-length pattern, same solver, 3 seeds. Cost $1, Sonnet.
2. Vigenère/Beaufort with periodic keys from the names (HARRY, CAROLINE, the other's name as key, a lovers' convention Gaffney documents) on each ad separately. Cost under $1.

3. Tissie-Jabber: treat as an enumeration: test 'day-of-week x hour' and 'race x horse number' by checking that the reply's set complements the first ad's set. Report the structure; no plaintext is expected. Cost under $1.
matched_control: English text of the same word-length pattern
value: low-moderate; Gaffney has read most of the genre, so what is left is short or a private code
status_24_Sept_2026: open per Schmeh 2017; no later solution found 24 Sept 2026
schema_note: cheap_tests_in_order are proposals (rule 10: an approach is not a claim); a test actually run is under cheap_test_done with its control

cheap_test_done.method: specs/cheap-tests/harry-caroline/run_test1.py -- tools/subst_hillclimb.py MASC with word boundaries, joint 74-letter (see letter-count note) Harry+Caroline text, t/u/g single-letter-word symbols fixed to a/I over all 8 combinations (max_homo=2, needed since 3 distinct symbols cannot all map into {a,i} under a strict 1:1 MASC), corpus tools/data/pg2701_mobydick.txt, restarts=15 iters=1500 seed=1
cheap_test_done.result: FAIL (negative) -- best combo {t:a,u:i,g:i} score_per_token=-1.005, reading 'ie ore tidinterea oun as leshing oth dthera a iisher i anddin rs i hate un ssten rods ho hsse'; tools/judge_plaintext.py FAILs on language (score=-1.442 vs null_p99=-1.848, real_p05=-0.919) though it clears letters and words checks; excluding Ebcvgfm from scoring (name variant) does not improve (score -1.049)
cheap_test_done.control: same solver/restarts/seed=1, real English words of the identical 20-word length pattern from tools/data/pg1661_holmes.txt (source distinct from the solver's own corpus), random 1:1 MASC, blind (no fixed symbols), 3 seeds: 33.8%, 31.1%, 16.2% letters correct
cheap_test_done.target_vs_control: target FAILs the language judge outright (never resembles English); control recovers 16-34% of letters blind on a same-design real-English MASC -- the setup can partially read a matched design, so the target's outright language FAIL is informative, not a tooling artifact
